lines.japanese:
「…………違う」
　そう、それはきっと違う。
　俺が死ねば本当に秋葉が助かるのならいい。
　けどそんな保証はどこにもないし、何より。
―――死が、救いになるなんて事はない。
　俺が死ぬことで秋葉が助かったにしても、その後で秋葉は何を思うだろう。
　悲しんでくれるのならいいが、それを罪として、一生ぬぐえない罪悪感として抱いてしまうのは違う。
　死が尊い、勇気ある決断なんていうのは違う。
　そんなもの―――ただ、現実から逃げるだけの手段にすぎない。
lines.label: s384
lines.maoEnglish:
“…No.” Yes. That couldn’t be right. If my death would truly save Akiha, then fine. But there was no guarantee it would—and more than anything…
Death could never be salvation.
Even if my death saved Akiha, how would she live with it afterward? I wouldn’t mind if she mourned me. But if she took my death for a sin and carried the guilt all her life, that would be wrong. There was nothing noble or courageous about choosing death. It was only another way to run from reality.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"………… Wrong."
Yes, it's probably wrong.
It's alright if I can really save Akiha by dying.
But there's no proof of that, and besides…
---I don't think death can be a way to save someone.
Even if Akiha is saved by my death, how would she feel afterwards?
It's fine if she only feels sad about it, but it's wrong if she should feel guilty for the rest of her life.
I don't think that choosing death is neither courageous nor honorable.
I think---that's just a way to run away from reality.

lines.japanese:
「あき、は……」
　秋葉はもう、以前の秋葉じゃない。
　彼女は人を殺すだけの生き物になってしまった。
　……けど、それでも生きていてほしいんだ。
　罪も罰も感じられない秋葉の代わりに、俺がそれを償うのなら――――秋葉は、生きていてもいいんだって、信じたい。
「…………いつか」
　いつか、元に戻れる日が来るなんて思えない。
　それでも信じ続ける事が、秋葉を守れなかった自分にできる最後の役割だった。

lines.maoEnglish: “Aki…ha…” Akiha was no longer the girl she had been. She had become a creature that did nothing but kill. …And still, I wanted her to live. If I could atone in her place for the guilt and punishment she could no longer feel, then I wanted to believe she had the right to go on living. “…Someday.” I couldn’t imagine a day when she would return to herself. But believing in that day was the last thing left to me, after I had failed to protect her.

　まあ、かといって別にやる事があったわけじゃない。
　ここで、こうして。
　自分の名前さえ忘れて午睡するのも、そうおかしな事ではないだろう。

After breakfast I had wandered into the woods and stretched out in the grass; perhaps that had been my mistake. Not that I had anything else to do. Here, like this, an afternoon nap deep enough to forget even my own name hardly seemed so strange.

lines.maoEnglish:

She did not live there. She merely existed: a doll in the fullest sense of the word.
